newsitem.title: BARBADOS: CRICKET-JADEJA RESCUES INDIA WITH FIGHTING 68.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JADEJA RESCUES INDIA WITH FIGHTING 68.

text.p: BRIDGETOWN, Barbados, May 3 (reuter) - Ajay Jadeja rescued India with a fine half-century against West Indies in the fourth and final one-day iternational at Kensington Oval on Saturday.
India, reeling on six for two after being put in to bat, recovered to make 199 for seven from their 50 overs on a placid pitch.
The touring team need victory to square the series which West Indies lead 2-1.
Jadeja made a fluent 68 off 78 balls, hitting four fours, and there were useful contributions from Mohammad Azharuddin (40), Rahul Dravid (30) and Robin Singh (29).
West Indies' captain Courtney Walsh was the most successful bowler with two for 26, including the prized scalp of Sachin Tendulkar.
The Indian skipper was brilliantly caught at first slip by Brian Lara in the fifth over of the innings for just a single.
This left India on six for two as Curtly Ambrose, in his first over, took his 199th wicket in one-day internationals when he bowled opener Saurav Ganguly for four.
Dravid and Azharuddin added 56 for the third wicket to revive the innings but both were dismissed as India crawled to 100 in 33.1 overs.
Jadeja and Singh featured in a fifth-wicket stand of 75 to bring a measure of respectability to India's total.
Walsh ended Jadeja's battling half-century when he produced a perfect yorker to rip out the middle stump with the first delivery of the 49th over.
